newsitem.title: UK: UK's TSMSi does Internet ad deal with MoneyWorld.
newsitem.headline: UK's TSMSi does Internet ad deal with MoneyWorld.

text.p: Britain's biggest Internet advertising sales house announced on Thursday a deal with financial Websites that it said would boost advertising revenue on the Internet.

TSMSi, a newly-created Internet division of Britain's largest television advertising sales house, TSMS, said it reached an agreement with a Website group called MoneyWorld and another financial Website.

TSMSi said it had agreed to sell advertising space on MoneyWorld's Website -- located at www.moneyworld.co.uk -- and other financial websites as part of a "Smarter Investor" bundle to be presented to British ad agencies and Internet sales houses.
TSMSi is a newly formed unit of United News & Media Plc .

In some cases TSMSi sells advertising space directly to advertisers or sponsors, but in other cases it says it bundles together similar Websites and sells advertising space to ad agencies and a growing number of new Internet "media buyers".

"We're building critical mass. It's good news for Website owners. It's good news for advertisers. And it's good news for advertisers' agencies," Paul Simon, the general manager of TSMSi, told Reuters.
He said the "Smarter Investor" package meant Internet media buyers could easily target Britain's "AB Men audience" -- professional men at the top of the socio-economic scale.

MoneyWorld describes itself as the "UK's Personal Finance Website", with financial news and information provided by 21 journalists and "finance professionals". The group said it was independent and not owned by any other company.

MoneyWorld's editor, Danny Bowers, said in a statement, "We are convinced (TSMSi's) expertise in the new media marketplace will allow MoneyWorld to significantly increase its return from advertising revenue."
Simon told Reuters another financial Website that had been "bundled" into TSMSi's "Smarter Investor" package was called Electronic Share Information -- located at www.esi.co.uk..
The Website for Cambridge-based ESI says it offers investors real-time share prices, portfolio management and an "online trading gateway".
TSMSi -- a part of TSMS, which sells advertising space for Britain's ITV television network -- was created recently to sell advertising space on the Internet and other new media.
TSMSi unit said in February that British companies spent less than one million pounds on Internet advertising in 1996, but it expected the figure to rise to close to 90 million pounds by 2000.
